Definition: to press upon, i.e. oppress, defraud, violate, overflow
BiblicalUsage: To oppress is to press a man down and keep him down, and the prophets name it as plainly as the law forbids it. The law says thou shalt not oppress an hired servant that is poor and needy, Amos cries against the cows of Bashan who oppress the poor and crush the needy, the Preacher sees the tears of the oppressed with no comforter, and Samuel asks the people, whom have I defrauded, whom have I oppressed?
TheologicalSignificance: I believe oppression is the sin the prophets never let go of, because it is the sin of the strong against the weak, and God hears the tears of the oppressed even when no man comforts them. Samuel could ask the question and get silence for an answer, and I hold that the ruler who can ask it is the ruler God is pleased with.
